extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for how examiners and applicants must handle amendments and other replies during patent prosecution, including after final rejection and after allowance, with required notices, timing, and form requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should immediately inspect amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions by applicant, especially those filed near the end of the period for reply, should be inspected immediately upon filing to determine whether they are completely responsive to the preceding Office action so as to prevent abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All amended applications forwarded to the examiner should be inspected at once to determine: (A) proper signature (MPEP § 714.01(a)); (B) filed within statutory/shortened period or time limit (MPEP § 710–§ 710.05); (C) fully responsive and complies with 37 CFR 1.121 (MPEP § 714.03 and § 714.04); (D) whether changes warrant transfer (MPEP § 903.08(d)); (E) whether application is special (MPEP § 708.01); (F) if claims suggested for interference have been copied (Chapter 2300); (G) traversal of a restriction requirement (MPEP § 818.03(a)); (H) use of non-permanent ("easily erasable") paper (MPEP § 714.07); (I) applicant-cited references (MPEP § 707.05(b) and § 1302.12); (J) terminal disclaimer filed (MPEP § 804.02, § 804.03, and § 1490); (K) any security-related matter added (MPEP § 115). If amendment is inadequate and sufficient time remains, applicant should be notified and warned to complete reply (see MPEP § 714.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental action when amendment reaches TC late
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental action may be necessary when an amendment is filed on or before the mailing date of the regular action but reaches the Technology Center later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplemental action should be promptly prepared, need not reiterate all portions of the previous action still applicable but must specify which portions to be disregarded and point out that the period for reply runs from the mailing of the supplemental action. The action should be headed 'Responsive to amendment of (date) and supplemental to the action mailed (date).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent ink and non-permanent paper rule (37 CFR 1.52(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.52(a) requires 'permanent dark ink or its equivalent' on papers that become part of the record; 'easily erasable' paper violates the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-permanence is discovered when amendment reaches TC or later, applicant must be promptly notified that the amendment is not entered and is required to file a permanent copy within 1 month or order the PTO to make a copy at applicant's expense. If no reply within 1 month, the PTO may make a copy and charge applicant. If discovered only when application is reached for action, include requirement for permanent copy in the Office action and do not hold up action. Good photocopies or facsimiles on satisfactory paper are acceptable in many cases; see MPEP § 608.01 for acceptable copies and related precedents (e.g., In re Application Papers Filed Jan. 20, 1956).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees must be paid before consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is required to pay excess claims fees for each claim in excess of allowable counts (e.g., in excess of 3 independent claims or in excess of 20 total claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees for proper multiple dependent claims are calculated based on the number of claims to which the multiple dependent claim refers (37 CFR 1.75(c)); a separate fee is required in each application containing a proper multiple dependent claim. When applicant adds a new excess claim in excess of the number of claims previously paid for (after cancellations), applicant must pay required excess claims fees before the examiner considers the new claim. Example provided illustrating recalculation after cancellations and additions. See MPEP § 607 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments during interference or reexamination follow special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed during interference proceedings or reexaminations are governed by special MPEP chapters and CFR provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For amendments filed during interference proceedings, see MPEP Chapter 2300. Amendments in ex parte or inter partes reexamination proceedings after final action are limited by 37 CFR 1.116 and related provisions; inter partes reexamination has narrower allowances (see 37 CFR 1.116(d)(1),(2) and (f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: What amendments/replies are permitted after final (37 CFR 1.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.116 governs amendments and affidavits/evidence after final action and prior to appeal; only certain amendments are allowed as of right or upon showing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted: (b)(1) amendments canceling claims or complying with form requirements expressly set forth; (b)(2) amendments presenting rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal may be admitted; (b)(3) amendments touching the merits may be admitted upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why necessary and not earlier presented. Affidavits or other evidence after final may be admitted under 1.116(e) only with good and sufficient reasons. Admission or refusal does not relieve the proceeding from appeal status or abandonment rules (see 1.135 and related).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after final are not a matter of right; showing expected
rubrics_metrics.description: After a final rejection that is not premature, applicant no longer has a right to unrestricted further prosecution; entry of amendments is discretionary and certain showings are expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except where amendment merely cancels claims, adopts examiner suggestions, or removes issues for appeal, compliance with the showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b)(3) is expected in all amendments after final rejection. An affidavit or other evidence filed after final (but before or on same date as appeal) may be entered only upon showing good and sufficient reasons under 37 CFR 1.116(e). Failure to properly reply under 37 CFR 1.113 results in abandonment. A reply under 37 CFR 1.113 is limited to: (A) an amendment complying with 37 CFR 1.116; (B) a Notice of Appeal and fee; or (C) an RCE filed under 37 CFR 1.114 with an appropriate submission and fee. RCE practice has specified exceptions (e.g., not for utility/plant apps filed before June 8, 1995 and not for design applications). Continued prosecution may be obtained for designs by CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action and explanation when amendment not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposed amendment does not place the case in better form for appeal or in condition for allowance, the examiner should promptly inform applicant and the refusal should not be arbitrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendment should be given sufficient consideration to determine if claims are in condition for allowance or if appeal issues are simplified. Ordinarily specific deficiencies need not be discussed, but if the amendment raises new matter, the examiner should identify the subject matter that constitutes new matter. If amendment presents new issues requiring further consideration/search, provide explanation. Reasons for non-entry should be concise: (A) amendment would not avoid rejections and thus not place case in condition for allowance or for appeal; (B) amendment raises new matter; (C) amendment presents new issues requiring further consideration/search; (D) amendment presents additional claims without canceling finally rejected claims and thus does not place case in better condition for appeal. Examiners should indicate status of each claim of record or proposed and which proposed claims would be entered on filing of an appeal if filed in a separate paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Advisory Action (PTOL-303) and form paragraph 7.169 for appeal entries
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant files a reply after final rejection that does not place the application in condition for allowance but is prior to filing an appeal brief, the Advisory Action form PTOL-303 should be used to advise applicant of disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.169 ('Advisory Action, Proposed Rejection of Claims, Before Appeal Brief') may be used to notify applicant that proposed amendment(s) will be entered upon appeal and how new/amended claims would be rejected. The advisory should identify claim groups and reference the rejection (e.g., 35 U.S.C. § 103 based on A in view of B) and advise that such rejections must be addressed in any brief on appeal. Use PTOL-303 to acknowledge receipt and disposition and to indicate which rejections will be included in Examiner's Answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness expectations for examiner processing of amendments after final
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are expected to promptly consider amendments filed after final and adhere to internal timing goals for responses and mailings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner is expected to turn in a response to an amendment after final rejection within 10 calendar days from receipt by examiner. A reply to an amendment after final should be mailed within 30 days of the date the amendment is received by the Office. If application is placed in condition for allowance, applicant should be notified promptly by Notice of Allowability (PTOL-37). If delays in processing Notice of Allowability are expected and statutory reply period is near, notify applicant by interview and mail Examiner Initiated Interview Summary PTOL-413B. Prompt notice is important to avoid unnecessary appeal or abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: One post-final interview policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution before the examiner should ordinarily be concluded with the final action, but one personal interview by applicant may be entertained after such final action if circumstances warrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one request by applicant for a personal interview after final should be granted; in exceptional circumstances, a second personal interview may be initiated by the examiner if it would materially assist in placing the application in condition for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection — shortened statutory period wording and fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific wording must be included in each final rejection setting a shortened statutory period for reply and explaining how extension fees are calculated when the advisory action is delayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph language (examples 7.39, 7.40, 7.41, etc.) must state that shortened statutory period to expire three months from mailing, but where a first reply is filed within two months and the advisory is not mailed until after the end of the three-month period, the shortened period will expire on the date the advisory action is mailed and extension fees will be calculated from that mailing date; in no event later than six months from the date of final rejection. Examples clarify calculations. Failure to file a reply during shortened period results in abandonment unless time extended under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand delivery and Customer Window requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Hand-carried papers for Technology Centers must be delivered to the Customer Window at the specified PTO address; some hand-carried submissions (e.g., after-final amendments) will no longer be accepted at TCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective Dec 1, 2003, all official patent application related correspondence for organizations reporting to the Commissioner of Patents that is hand-carried must be delivered to the Customer Window (Randolph Building, 401 Dulany Street, Alexandria, VA). Hand-carried amendments and other replies after final rejection (37 CFR 1.116) will no longer be accepted in the TCs; couriers will be redirected to the Customer Window. Patent-application-related CDs and non-paper hand-carried submissions must also be delivered to Customer Window. See MPEP § 502.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited procedure for processing replies under 37 CFR 1.116 (Mail Stop AF)
rubrics_metrics.description: An expedited processing procedure exists for amendments and replies under 37 CFR 1.116 if applicant follows specified marking and routing instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain expedited processing, mark the amendment or reply 'Reply under 37 CFR 1.116 — Expedited Procedure - Technology Center (Insert Technology Center Number)' on the upper right of the paper and mark the envelope 'Mail Stop AF' in the lower left. Prefer bright color marking. If mailed, the envelope should contain only replies under 1.116 and be mailed to 'Mail Stop AF, Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia, 22313-1450.' Hand-carried replies may be delivered to the Customer Window. Upon proper receipt, envelope will be specially processed and forwarded promptly to the examining TC; the Office's goal is to mail the examiner's action on the reply within 1 month from receipt. Applicants are encouraged to use the procedure; if not used, benefits will not be attained. If no action within expected time plus normal mailing, contact SPE or TC Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after allowance governed by 37 CFR 1.312 (no right to amend)
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may be made as a matter of right after mailing of the notice of allowance; any amendment must comply with 37 CFR 1.312 and be filed before or with payment of issue fee to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after allowance may be entered on recommendation of the primary examiner approved by the Director (delegated to SPE). Examples of 'amendments' include (A) specification amendment, (B) change in drawings, (C) amendment to claims, (D) change in inventorship, (E) submission of prior art, (F) petition to correct spelling of inventor's name, (G) petition to change order of inventors, etc. An amendment under 1.312 must be filed on or before the date the issue fee is paid (except where required by Office of Patent Publication). Entries that merely correct formal matters without changing scope or that cancel claims may be entered by primary examiner; other amendments require SPE approval. If amendment is non-compliant with 1.121 but would otherwise be recommended, examiner may enter and correct non-compliance via examiner's amendment. See MPEP § 714.16 and § 714 generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for entering amendments under 37 CFR 1.312
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments after allowance should be considered only where they are needed for proper disclosure/protection and require no substantial additional work by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Technology Center Director may set policy regarding trivial informalities. Consideration of an amendment under 1.312 cannot be demanded as a matter of right. For amendments affecting disclosure, scope of any claim, or adding a claim, remarks accompanying the amendment must fully and clearly state: (A) why the amendment is needed; (B) why the proposed amended or new claims require no additional search or examination; (C) why the claims are patentable; and (D) why they were not presented earlier. The requirements of 37 CFR 1.111(c) (pointing out patentable novelty) apply. Examiner may recommend entry only if these showings are satisfactory and entry would not require substantial Office work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quayle action and closure of prosecution after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: After all claims in an application have been allowed (Ex parte Quayle), prosecution on the merits is closed; amendments touching merits after allowance are treated similarly to amendments after final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.51 (Quayle Action) to issue notice that application is in condition for allowance except for specified formal matters and that prosecution on the merits is closed. A shortened statutory period for reply is set to expire TWO MONTHS from mailing. Amendments that touch the merits after allowance fall under 37 CFR 1.312 procedures and are a matter of grace, not right. See MPEP § 714.14–§ 714.16.
